about_blocks.text: About Red Road North in Terrace, BC
about_blocks.html: About Red Road North in Terrace, BC

about_blocks.text: Red Road North is a residential addiction treatment centre for adults outside Terrace, in Northwest British Columbia. Red Road Recovery, a CARF-accredited operator with homes in Sorrento, Lumby and Salmon Arm, runs it in partnership with the Northern First Nations Alliance (NFNA). The house has 12 beds and sits on a riverfront acreage on Highway 16 East, along the Skeena River.
about_blocks.html: Red Road North is a residential addiction treatment centre for adults outside Terrace, in Northwest British Columbia. Red Road Recovery, a CARF-accredited operator with homes in Sorrento, Lumby and Salmon Arm, runs it in partnership with the Northern First Nations Alliance (NFNA). The house has 12 beds and sits on a riverfront acreage on Highway 16 East, along the Skeena River.

about_blocks.text: The centre held its grand opening on December 2, 2025. Representatives from Red Road Recovery, the Nisga'a Lisims Government and Kitsumkalum Health attended. In March 2026 the Province named Red Road North's 12 land-based treatment beds as part of its Indigenous Treatment and Recovery Program.

about_blocks.text: Treatment follows the same model Red Road Recovery uses at its other homes. Residents take part in individual and group counselling, recovery education and practical skill building, with an introduction to the 12 Steps. Cultural programming is shaped by local Indigenous partners and can include smudging, medicine wheel teachings, land-based activities, time with Elders and Knowledge Keepers, and sweat lodge ceremonies. Red Road Recovery says all of its staff have personal experience of recovery.

about_blocks.text: Programs run for 30, 45, 60 or 90 days, and news coverage of the Terrace location described a 90-day program. The program is co-ed and for adults 19 and over, and the residence is staffed around the clock. Meals come from in-house chefs.

about_blocks.text: Terrace is in the Skeena region of Northern BC, about 15 hours by road from Vancouver or under two hours by air to Northwest Regional Airport (Terrace-Kitimat). Kitimat, Prince Rupert, the Nass Valley and the Hazeltons are all within a few hours' drive, which makes Red Road North the closest Red Road Recovery home for much of the northwest coast and interior.

about_blocks.text: Red Road Recovery offers several ways to pay. Publicly funded beds are open to BC residents over 19 at no cost. Private beds can be paid by the person, family, a First Nations band, insurance or an employer, and FNHA subsidy, contracted beds for bands and Medicard financing are also listed. Prices are given on request.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Red Road North

faqs.question: What kind of program is Red Road North?

answer_blocks.text: Red Road North is a 12-bed residential addiction treatment centre for adults, run by Red Road Recovery in partnership with the Northern First Nations Alliance (NFNA). Residents live on site, and Red Road Recovery says its residences are staffed 24/7. The home is registered with the BC assisted living registry as a supportive recovery residence, and the treatment program holds CARF accreditation.
answer_blocks.html: Red Road North is a 12-bed residential addiction treatment centre for adults, run by Red Road Recovery in partnership with the Northern First Nations Alliance (NFNA). Residents live on site, and Red Road Recovery says its residences are staffed 24/7. The home is registered with the BC assisted living registry as a supportive recovery residence, and the treatment program holds CARF accreditation.

answer_blocks.text: Red Road North is at 20047 Highway 16 East, on a riverfront acreage outside Terrace in Northwest BC. Local news coverage places it on the Skeena River. Terrace is about 15 hours by road from Vancouver, so most people from the Lower Mainland fly into Northwest Regional Airport (Terrace-Kitimat).

faqs.question: How much does Red Road North cost?

answer_blocks.text: Red Road Recovery does not publish prices; it asks you to contact the team for private pricing. It also lists publicly funded beds at no cost for BC residents over 19, funded through a CMHA grant, with 23 such beds across its network. Private stays can be paid by the person, family, a First Nations band, insurance or an employer.

faqs.question: Can First Nations clients get funding?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. Red Road Recovery says subsidy for its program is available through the First Nations Health Authority (FNHA), and First Nation bands can buy contracted beds at a discounted rate to avoid waitlists. The Province also announced in March 2026 that Red Road North's 12 land-based treatment beds are part of its Indigenous Treatment and Recovery Program.

answer_blocks.text: The residential program is co-ed and for adults 19 and over. Publicly funded beds require BC residency, while privately funded beds are open to anyone. The Nisga'a Lisims Government's coverage of the opening said the centre was built with Northwest First Nations communities in mind, and Red Road Recovery does not publish any other eligibility limits.

faqs.question: Does Red Road North offer detox?

answer_blocks.text: Red Road Recovery's own website does not describe a detox or withdrawal management service at Red Road North, and recovery.com lists detox as not offered. A December 2025 article from the Nisga'a Lisims Government mentioned withdrawal management, so call 250-800-3190 to ask what medical support is in place before you arrive.
